s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal and pelvic pain with a renal mass and vascular involvement
salient_findings: Right renal mass with fat attenuation
Fatty tumor thrombus in the right renal vein
key_facts: 66-year-old woman
History of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma
Abdominal and pelvic pain
Unremarkable physical examination
Normal laboratory studies
Normal creatinine level of 0.81 mg dl–1
Right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation
Defect in the renal parenchyma
Visible vessels extending into the renal cortex
Fatty tumor thrombus in the right renal vein
Thrombus extending to the confluence with the inferior vena cava
No other masses or enlarged lymph nodes identified

shortlist.label: Renal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Renal mass with areas of fat attenuation and vascular involvement

shortlist.label: Angiomyolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of fat attenuation within the renal mass

shortlist.label: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of renal cell carcinoma with vascular involvement

shortlist.label: Renal metastasis from endometrial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma

shortlist.label: Renal epithelioid angiomyolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor with vascular involvement and potential for fat attenuation

raw.rationale: The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation and a fatty tumor thrombus in the right renal vein is highly suggestive of angiomyolipoma, a benign tumor that can contain fat and vessels.

rejected.label: Renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of fat attenuation within the tumor is more characteristic of angiomyolipoma than renal cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma is a subtype of renal cell carcinoma and does not typically contain fat attenuation.

rejected.label: Renal metastasis from endometrial carcinoma
rejected.why: Metastases to the kidney from endometrial carcinoma are rare and would not typically present with fat attenuation within the tumor.

rejected.label: Renal epithelioid angiomyolipoma
rejected.why: While this is a subtype of angiomyolipoma, the provided information does not specifically suggest epithelioid characteristics, making angiomyolipoma a more general and appropriate diagnosis based on the given details.
